query_database.py:122-123 computes fence = max(3, 1+longest backtick run in sql). CommonMark closes a backtick fence only with a run at least as long as the opener, indented at most 3 spaces, followed only by whitespace. Every backtick run inside the SQL, indented or not, is strictly shorter than the fence, so none can close the block. Only the final fence line closes it. The info string 'sql' has no backticks, so the opener is valid. I traced this from the CommonMark rules and the implementation. I did not read or run the test renderer.

query_database.py:122 sets the fence to max(3, 1 + longest backtick run in sql). Per CommonMark a closing fence needs at least as many backticks as the opener, so no run in the SQL, indented 0-3 spaces or not, can close it. A `~~~` line inside a backtick fence is plain content, because only backtick fences close backtick fences. The info string 'sql' has no backticks. The closing fence is at column 0 on its own line (line 123). The test at test_output_boundaries.py:49 covers runs 3/4/8 and checks the rendered output.
